feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: Breaking news, top national and world stories, politics, business and culture from NPR. Catch up on demand with NPR News Now, Up First and Consider This.

entry.title: New book revisits the 2023 killing of an unhoused man in crisis on the NYC subway
entry.summary: Jordan Neely was frightening fellow passengers. A former Marine named Daniel Penny put Neely into a chokehold, killing him. Journalist Anand Giridharadas investigates the incident in Man in the Mirror.

entry.title: Fed holds interest rates steady even as inflation remains stubborn
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve opted to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged — but investors widely expect the central bank to raise rates at its next meeting in December to combat stubborn inflation.

entry.title: Dolores Huerta, influential labor leader, feminist and civil rights icon, dies at 96
entry.summary: Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union to improve working conditions in the nation's fruit and vegetable fields and coined the phrase "Sí, se puede!" that became a widespread rallying cry.

entry.title: What's gone up even faster than gas or rent? The cost of caregiving
entry.summary: A new study from AARP shows caregivers' out-of-pocket costs rose about 60% in the last five years.

entry.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
entry.summary: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

entry.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
entry.summary: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.

entry.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
entry.summary: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

entry.title: Partnerships between ICE and local police surge, report finds
entry.summary: The number of state and local officers working with Immigration and Customs Enforcement has doubled in size in the last eight months, according to a new report from the immigration reform advocacy group FWD.us.

entry.title: New teachers union president wants to steer educators away from partisan politics
entry.summary: NEA President Princess Moss wants to move her organization, the nation's largest labor union, toward issue-based advocacy — and away from party politics.

entry.title: Why many student voters have a right to choose where to register to vote
entry.summary: Student voters studying outside their hometown have a right to choose where they register to vote. Advocates say a Montana legal fight is a reminder of a misunderstanding of those students' rights.
